newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses hit records, dollar rally fades.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses hit records, dollar rally fades.

text.p: European bourses moved ahead strongly on Wednesday, Frankfurt and Paris hitting new records, but a morning dollar rally faded, albeit leaving the U.S. currency well up against the mark and yen compared with Tuesday's prices.
The dollar slipped back in afternoon trading after scoring a 47-month high against the Swiss franc, surging well above the 1.84 mark level and hitting an 11-week peak in yen earlier in the day.

It was a bullish day for European stocks. Frankfurt closed both floor and electronic trading at record highs, Paris also scored a new closing high, 1.5 percent up on the day, and London, Europe's biggest bourse, ended over one percent higher.

Leading shares had been boosted by dollar strength, which helps European exporters, an overnight Wall Street rally and a higher opening for the Dow, which was up around 85 points or over one percent by the time European business ended.

By late afternoon in Europe, the dollar was around 118.40 yen, off its morning peaks but still above Tuesday's level. In morning trading it peaked at 118.95 yen after Japanese industrial output and retail sales data bolstered expectations that Japan's interest rates would stay near record lows for the time being.

"The dollar/yen did get to levels where we would expect some form of Bank of Japan or Ministry of Finance commentary in support of the yen and the 120 area will act as a barrier as a result," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.

Against the mark, the dollar broke through and moved well above the 1.84 level, despite speculation the Bundesbank could switch to using variable-rate tenders to set its securities repurchase rate. But by the end of European trading it had slipped back to around 1.8375. Against the Swiss franc the dollar touched 1.5259 before retracing to around 1.5170.

On the Frankfurt bourse the DAX index rose 40.3 points or 0.91 percent to chalk up a new record closing high at 4,421.72. Dealers said the overnight Wall Street gains and the strong dollar had underpinned sentiment.
Banking stocks, including Vereinsbank BWMG.F and Deutsche Bank, featured strongly in the rally.
Frankfurt electronic trade, measured by the IBIS DAX index, also closed above its previous life high, set on July 24.
It was a similar story in Paris, which opened at a new record high, also supported by Wall Street and the dollar, and continued to trade in record territory.
The main CAC-40 index closed up 45.67 at 3069.3, well above its previous trading record of 3044.24.
Pharmaceutical and beauty products group Sanofi continued its strong rise from Tuesday on expectations it will sell its 49.9 percent stake in the Nina Ricci perfume business.

In London, Europe's biggest stock exchange, the leading FTSE 100 share index rose sharply and was given a further boost when Wall Street moved ahead in early trading. Gains in the banking, oil and retail sectors helped it close more than one percent up at 4927.3, still well under its life high of 4998.1, set on July 18.

London traders said they would remain cautious until this week's UK earnings reports were completed and a batch of U.S. economic figures had been released, culminating on Friday with July unemployment data.
"We started off on the back of Wall Street...but people are keeping their powder dry and not strongly committing one way or the other," one trader said.
"We've got eight FTSE companies reporting this week, three already, and the (U.S.) non-farm payrolls on Friday, so there is a bit of caution at this point," he added.

Dealers said the progress of sterling remained a focus after the currency's four percent slide against major currencies this week gave a major boost to exporters. The pound bounced off Tuesday's lows and by late Wednesday sterling/mark was trading at around 2.9960, up from 2.9830 late in Europe on Tuesday.
Dealers said sterling appeared to have paused for breath, setting its sights firmly on re-taking the 3.0 mark level after its two-day slide knocked it over eight pfennigs lower.
"The sell-off was a bit like a shower. Sterling had a knock-back but the sun is out and the umbrella is back down," said a trader at a European bank.

The pound, which has climbed from as low as 2.2755 marks in August 1996, has been spirited higher by a cocktail of factors including strong domestic growth, higher interest rates and its status as a safe haven currency if a broad-based single European currency is launched.

The market is now focusing on the Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee meeting next week to see if the central bank will raise rates. Data showing a record rise in personal credit in June highlight the need for higher rates, some analysts believe.
"Rates are going higher," said one trader at a European bank. "If not next week, then in September."

Elsewhere in currencies traders had been expecting the dollar to claw back ground it lost to the mark on Tuesday, after its surge to a seven-and-a-half-year peak of 1.8490 on Monday triggered profit taking.
"We tend to go up by the stairs and down by the lift these days but there is good demand for dollars after yesterday's correction and we should grind higher," said a trader in London.

Meanwhile, on the London metal exchange, volatile zinc prices were recovering after a headlong plunge on Tuesday. LME benchmark three-month zinc ended around 1,450 dollars a tonne on Wednesday on residual tightness, "but there is more stormy weather to come in the zinc market," one trader said.
On Tuesday zinc's recent surge ended abruptly when speculators liquidated their positions, pushing three-month zinc down 300 dollars per tonne to a low of 1,370 dollars.
CURRENCIES AT 1545 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8375 marks and 118.40 yen compared with 1.8299 and 117.82 in late trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed up 50.7 points at 4,927.3.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index closed up 40.03 points in bourse trade at 4,421.72.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed up 45.67 points at 3,069.30.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed in the afternoon at $327.55 compared with London's close on Tuesday of 326.45. Silver was at $4.40.
